mistakes: None. It was a calendar-only day with no chart, levels, setups or watchlist, so there was nothing to break.
This review covers price action from web reports, not OANDA fills. No trades have been pasted from the Journal yet, so review.trades is left empty.

Price data was too thin to judge any break and retest. Web sources only gave snapshot quotes (EUR/USD about 1.097, GBP/USD about 1.310, USD/JPY about 159.1 in the London morning) and no M5/M15 candles, so it can't be said whether any pair produced an A or B setup after the 07:00 release.
lessons: Repeat: Standing aside without a chart was the right call. With no marked levels there is nothing to grade a break and retest against, and both news blocks (05:30 CAD Retail Sales, 07:00 USD UoM Sentiment) covered the start of the window for every USD pair.

Improve tomorrow: The dollar is near a 19-month high (DXY about 103.8) going into the weekend, with EUR/USD near its lowest since April 2025 and GBP/USD near a one-year low. On Monday, mark those lows plus the Friday highs and lows as H1 levels, and post a chart so the plan has levels to grade. Canada's September retail sales beat (+0.8%), but the October flash was -1.5%, so watch USD/CAD around its recent range.

Most profit: No plan setups or pasted trades today, so there is no R to compare. The edge on a calendar-only day comes from the Opening Range signals taken after the news blocks clear, at the signal's price, stop and target.
review.gradingAudit: No setups were graded today because there was no chart, so there is nothing to audit. Standing aside fits the rules: no levels means no break and retest can be scored.
